## Design

### 2026-11-05: At the start of this session, I did a lot of research on what components I should use. This isn't something I've done much of because I've been following a lot of starter projects, so it took me a whi

**7h**

At the start of this session, I did a lot of research on what components I should use. This isn't something I've done much of because I've been following a lot of starter projects, so it took me a while. I was originally planning on using a seperate charging circuit and voltage converter, but I ended up finding an ESP32 devboard that has both of these integrated, so all I have to do is connect the battery to it and it should all work. I chose to go with an 18650 battery for this project because I already have some and they have good capacity. I also chose a 2.4 in tft screen for the display.

Most components I'm using don't have Kicad files, so I had to make my own. I had to do this for the esp32 devboard, the screen, and the toggle switch that I'm using for power. Figuring out the spacings for all the pins was pretty hard because I had to look up the documents with the components dimensions to properly model them. The devboard I'm using doesn't give exact dimensions or pin spacings, so I assumend it uses standard arduino dupont spacing. This took me a while because I don't have much experience doing this, but I think they ended up pretty good.

After this, i started wiring up the schematic. I had to do a good bit of research about which pins of the esp32 I could connect to because the listing for the devboard I'm using wasn't very descriptive. I ended up needing pullup resistors for 4/7 of the buttons because they are connected to pins that don't have internal pullups. I also went ahead and wired up the sd card portion of the screen even though I don't plan on using it, Just in case.

Overall, I'm really enjoying making a project without a beginner's guide. I think its really cool to see everything I've learned over the past 4 weeks come to help me design my very own project from scratch! Although it's taking a lot longer than it did with the guides, I am very happy with the progress I've made so far and can't wait to continue this project!

### 2026-11-06: In this session I laid out the components in the PCB editor and routed the traces.

**3h**

In this session I laid out the components in the PCB editor and routed the traces.

When first laying out the components, I had the esp32 and the battery at the bottom, but I didn't like the way this looked because It gave the device a missive chin, so I moved the battery between the buttons and the screen to even it out a bit.

After this, I did all the routing of the traces. When I was almost done, I realized I had the esp32 on backwards and wouldn't be able to plug in the USB port, so i pretty much had to start again from scratch. The traces still don't look great, but they look a lot better than they did for some of my previous projects. I think one way to help make the easier would be to keep the layout and traces in mind when creating the schematic, which is something I haven't been doing because the schematic in itself is already pretty difficult for me.

After routing the traces and making the board edge, I did a little decoration and the PCB was done! Now I need to design the enclosure for it and write the firmware.

### 2026-11-06: In this session I 3d modeled the case for the project. One of the biggest issues I ran into during this process was that the battery was a lot bigger than I thought it was, so I had to design a little

**3h**

In this session I 3d modeled the case for the project. One of the biggest issues I ran into during this process was that the battery was a lot bigger than I thought it was, so I had to design a little bump in the case to make room for it. Because if this, I will have to raise the screen up using arduino headers. This isn't shown in the 3d model because I don't really care enough to go edit the PCB 3d model when I know what it's supposed to look like.

The case is made out of two parts, the bottom and the top. Because of the bump I had to add to the top, it might be a little tricky to print, but it should end up fine with the supports. The bottom should have no issue at all printing.

Overall I'm getting much more comfortable 3d modeling and I can't wait to see how this project turns out! Now all I need to do is write the firmware, which I'm kind of dreading doing because it's really complicated and going to take a WHILE. However, I have an idea to make it more interesting, so stay tuned....

### 2026-11-06: Spent a while in the Arduino IDE this session. I feel like I've been coding all day and I'm only half way done, this is gonna take a while. using the TFT screen isn't awful, but it's new for me so I'm

**6h**

Spent a while in the Arduino IDE this session. I feel like I've been coding all day and I'm only half way done, this is gonna take a while. using the TFT screen isn't awful, but it's new for me so I'm having to do a lot of googling and reading forums to figure out exactly what I'm supposed to be doing again. I took the button debouncing code from one of my other weeks and used that instead of making it from scratch again. I also was able to reuse the code from my midi keypad that controls the rotary encoder, which definitely saved me some time. I've gotten a bit more comfortable with all the wifi stuff on the ESP32 recently because I've done a couple of projects with it, so it's been nice to have at least that part go faster. I think I'm going to try to have everything done by tomorrow afternoon, so I've got a LOT of work left to do tomorrow. Hopefully my fingers can haldle more typing tomorrow lol. I've still got an idea on how to test the code, but I want to get closer to finishing before I try that.
